**🚀 Performance & Scalability** | **🟠 Major** | **🏗️ Heavy lift**

Each footnote triggers two full scans of the document:

Fix:
- Keep a running footnote counter instead of calling `countNotes()`.
- A pending note's marker can only be in blocks added since the last flush, or in the open table and row buffers. Remember the `doc_.body` index from before the flush. Then limit `replaceNoteId()` to `[startIndex, doc_.body.size())` plus `bodyRuns_`, `rowCells_` and `table_`.

title: Footnote resolution still scales quadratically when many notes are pending in one flush.
body:
**🚀 Performance & Scalability** | **🟠 Major** | **🏗️ Heavy lift**

**Footnote resolution still scales quadratically when many notes are pending in one flush.**

The `noteScanFrom_` change fixes the case of one note per paragraph. It does not fix the case where many notes resolve in the same `resolveNotes` call.

- `resolveNotes` calls `replaceNoteId` once per note. Each call scans every block from `start`, plus `bodyRuns_`, `rowCells_` and `table_`.
- In `onlyInDocument` mode, `noteIdInDocument` also scans from `start` once per pending note.
- A single paragraph can hold about 100,000 `{\footnote x}` groups, which is roughly 1.3 MB of input. Each marker is a separate run, because `Fmt::matches` rejects runs that have a `noteId`.
- `resolveNotes` then processes all notes until `kMaxBlocks` rejects the input. The scan covers the paragraph's runs and the footnote blocks added so far, on every iteration. That is about 10^10 string comparisons before the parser reports an error.
- A table has the same problem. Notes stay pending until `pushTable`, and each scan walks the whole table block.

The 32 MiB and `kMaxBlocks` caps do not bound this cost. This violates the learning that imported input must be bounded.

Fix: replace the per-note scans with single passes.
1. In `resolveNotes`, collect the note IDs found in `doc_.body[start..]` once into a `QSet<QString>`. Use it for the `onlyInDocument` test.
2. While adding footnote blocks, record `tempId -> finalId` in a `QHash<QString, QString>`.
3. After the loop, run one `replaceNoteIds(map, start)` pass over the same ranges that `replaceNoteId` covers now. Look up each non-empty `r.noteId` in the map.

<details>
<summary>♻️ Sketch of the single-pass replacement</summary>

```diff
-    void replaceNoteId(const QString &from, const QString &to, int start)
+    void replaceNoteIds(const QHash<QString, QString> &map, int start)
     {
         auto fix = [&](QVector<TextRun> &runs) {
             for (TextRun &r : runs) {
-                if (r.noteId == from)
-                    r.noteId = to;
+                if (r.noteId.isEmpty())
+                    continue;
+                const auto it = map.constFind(r.noteId);
+                if (it != map.constEnd())
+                    r.noteId = it.value();
             }
         };
```

In `resolveNotes`, fill `map[note.tempId] = doc_.body.last().id` inside the loop. Call `replaceNoteIds(map, start)` once after the loop.
</details>

Note: nested notes must still resolve correctly with a single pass. Because the new `replaceNoteIds` runs after all footnote blocks exist, it also replaces markers inside note blocks added in the same call.

The traceback exits with code 1, which the docs define as "something to triage". The gate never reports `CLEAN`, `PENDING`, or any finding. The `--self-test` path calls `evaluate` directly and never reaches this line, so the `pr_merge_gate_selftest` ctest still passes.

```diff
+++ "b/scripts/pr-merge-gate.py"
@@ -275,7 +275,7 @@
     def refetch():
         return get(f"{API}/pulls/{args.pr}")
 
-    return _print_result(evaluate(args.pr, pr, statuses, comments, reviews, commit_date, args.since, refetch))
+    return _print_result(*evaluate(args.pr, pr, statuses, comments, reviews, commit_date, args.since, refetch))

```

title: Keep read-only exports from changing the working document.
body:

`src/core/Session.cpp:5399-5410` **🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | **🟠 Major** | **🏗️ Heavy lift** **Keep read-only exports from changing the working document.** When a dirty read-only document contains a stale statistic field, this gate permits `document_save`. `saveDocument` then calls `refreshIfFields(doc_, dirty_)`, which can replace the field’s stored text before export.
